dedupe_keys.name: epa incident waste decision support tool i waste dst

description: I-WASTE is the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's web tool for planning how to manage waste and debris from disasters and contamination incidents. It helps users estimate the mass and volume of waste generated from buildings such as offices, schools, theatres, shopping malls, homes, hotels and hospitals, find treatment and disposal facilities in national databases of landfills, combustion and hazardous waste sites, and look up information on contaminants, decontamination, worker safety, packaging, storage and transport. The provider is the EPA Office of Research and Development, with Eastern Research Group as the main contractor. Coverage is the United States, for incidents ranging from hurricanes and floods to chemical, biological and radiological contamination; during Hurricane Florence in 2018 it was used to estimate likely waste and to map waste facilities in North and South Carolina and Virginia against flood maps, so that communities could avoid sending debris to flooded landfills. Access is free through a web application with user accounts; 2020 training slides say first-time users must request a login and planned a move to cloud.gov servers. Results export to Excel, and saved scenarios can be shared. Caveats: EPA stresses that it is not an expert system and does not tell users what to do, the building estimates are rough, and facility lists need local confirmation. Simulation uses: debris quantity inputs for recovery logistics and landfill capacity scenarios after a disaster. Related records: the Florida marine debris lessons (case_study-florida-hurricane-marine-debris-2016-2017) report real debris volumes and costs.
